title: Finite separable base refinement
statement: Let $k\subseteq L$ be a finite separable field extension [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and let $q:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If the composite $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and projective [def-kun-projective], then $q$ is smooth and projective, and in particular proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0G80 (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-smooth-etale-permanence); Tag 0C4Q (morphisms.tex, lemma-projective-permanence), with Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), and Tag 01W9 (lemma-H-projective); properness: Tag 01WC (morphisms.tex, lemma-locally-projective-proper, lines 10579-10614)

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}L$, let $a:T\to S$ be induced by the inclusion, and put $f=a\circ q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], $a$ is etale, since $L/k$ is finite separable. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], $a$ is separated, since $T$ is affine.

Form $W=Z\times_S T$ with projections $r:W\to Z$ and $b:W\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any scheme $U$, maps $U\to W$ are pairs $(u:U\to Z,v:U\to T)$ with $f\circ u=a\circ v$. Reading this pair as $(v,u)$ shows that $(W,b,r)$ is also the fibre product of $(a,f)$, with second projection $r$. Thus the second-projection statements cited next apply to $r$ directly. The map $r$ is the base change of $a$ along $f$, so is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The identity $a\circ q=f$ defines $\gamma=(\mathrm{id}_Z,q):Z\to W$, with $r\circ\gamma=\mathrm{id}_Z$ and $b\circ\gamma=q$. The open-immersion argument of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] makes $\gamma$ an open immersion. Only this clause is needed: the section is a monomorphism, its composite with $r$ is the etale identity, so Etale.of_comp followed by IsOpenImmersion.of_flat_of_mono applies without needing separatedness of $r$.

source.place: Tag 024T, proposition-properties-sections; morphisms.tex, Tag 02GO; schemes.tex, Tag 01KU

proof.text: The map $b:W\to T$ is also the base change of the smooth map $f:Z\to S$ along $a$. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] therefore makes $b$ smooth. Since $\gamma$ is an open immersion, [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] makes $b\circ\gamma=q$ smooth. This proves smoothness without treating $q$ itself as the base change of $f$.

source.place: Tags 01VB, 01VC, 01VA (lemma-base-change-smooth, lemma-open-immersion-smooth, lemma-composition-smooth); alternative graph proof of more-morphisms.tex, Tag 0G80

proof.text: By [def-kun-projective], choose a finite homogeneous-coordinate type $n$ and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(n;S)$ whose structural composite is $f$. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] and [def-pc-fibre-product], the equality $\pi\circ i=f=a\circ q$ gives $j:Z\to\mathbf P(n;T)$, implemented by ProjectiveSpace.liftBaseChange q i. Its composites with the projection to $\mathbf P(n;S)$ and the structure map to $T$ are $i$ and $q$. The same finite coordinate type works over both fields, including the empty coordinate type.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, construction of the map into the base-changed projective bundle; finite projective space case

proof.text: The projection $p$ is the base change of the separated morphism $a$, hence is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. Since $p\circ j=i$ is a closed immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-cancellation] makes $j$ a closed immersion. The equality $h\circ j=q$ is then exactly an embedding into the finite projective space required by [def-kun-projective], so $q$ is projective.

source.place: Tag 07RK, lemma-immersion-permanence (3); Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence; schemes.tex, Tag 01KU, lemma-separated-permanence (3)

proof.text: Apply the already proved upstream instance AlgebraicGeometry.IsHProjective.isProper, the projective-to-proper assertion of [lem-pc-projective-proper], to the H-projectivity of $q$ from step 5. This instance factors through the closed immersion and the proper finite projective-space projection. Together with steps 3 and 5 this proves all three assertions. The separate sorry-bearing hProjective_properness theorem of lem-kun-projective-implies-proper is unnecessary.
